entry.title: Hausdorff dimension of union of lines that cover a curve
entry.summary: We construct a continuously differentiable curve in the plane that can be covered by a collection of lines such that every line intersects the curve at a single point and the union of the lines has Hausdorff dimension 1. We show that for twice differentiable curves this is impossible. In that case, the union of the lines must have Hausdorff dimension 2. If we use only tangent lines then the differentiability of the curve already implies that the union of the lines must have Hausdorff dimension 2, unless the curve is a line. We also construct a continuous curve, which is in fact the graph of a strictly convex function, such that the union of (one sided) tangent lines has Hausdorff dimension 1.
